item.title: 150k GPU-hours on Isambard-AI
item.description: Keith and I have been awarded 150k GPU-hours on Isambard-AI, the UK’s national AI supercomputer in Bristol, through UKRI’s AIRR AI Open Access call.

item.title: CrystaLLM-π workshop at the PSDI & Royce Materials Data Summit
item.description: Co-organised a lecture and hands-on workshop at the PSDI & Royce Materials Data Summit in Manchester, on how to use CrystaLLM-π to predict crystal structures. Notebooks are on github.

item.title: Conditional generative models enable targeted exploration of MAX phase design space
MAX phase paper out in J. Mater. Chem. C
item.description: Jamie’s paper is out in Journal of Materials Chemistry C. It uses CrystaLLM-π to explore the MAX phase design space.

item.title: Six Open Questions in Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential Foundation Models
Six open questions in MLIP foundation models
item.description: A perspective on foundation machine-learned interatomic potentials, written as a journal club as well as some other researchers in the field. We go through six questions we think will shape the area of MLIPs over the next few years.

item.title: Talk at AI4AM 2026 in Madrid
item.description: Gave a talk on CrystaLLM-π at the AI4AM 2026 conference in Madrid.

item.title: Poster at the IOP workshop on ML for experimental materials data
item.description: Presented CrystaLLM-π at the IOP workshop on Machine Learning for Experimental Materials Data in London.

item.title: Poster at the GeMMS 2026 Spring School
item.description: Presented a the CrystaLLM-π poster at the GeMMS 2026 Spring School in London. A week long of lectures, tutorials and research talks on deep generative models, including latent variable, diffusion, flow-based and autoregressive models.

item.title: CrystaLLM-π preprint is out
item.description: The CrystaLLM-π preprint is on arXiv! We inject continuous properties straight into the transformer’s attention, so the model keeps what it learned in pre-training while being steered towards a target. Example applications in the paper include recovering structures from X-ray diffraction patterns, and discover new photovoltaic candidates that we then checked with DFT.

item.title: Discovery and recovery of crystalline materials with property-conditioned transformers
Poster at the ML for Molecules and Materials school in Zadar
item.description: Attended the School on Machine Learning for Molecules and Materials Research in Zadar, Croatia. A week of lectures and tutorials, as well as a poster session where I presented CrystaLLM-Prop, predicting band gaps from CIFs with the original CrystaLLM.

item.title: Poster at the AIchemy annual conference
item.description: Brought the CrystaLLM-Prop poster to the first AIchemy annual conference, at Imperial’s White City campus in London. The project uses the original CrystaLLM to predict band gaps from CIFs.

item.title: Poster at the RSC Solid State Chemistry Christmas Meeting
item.description: My first conference poster of the PhD, at the 43rd RSC Solid State Chemistry Group Christmas Meeting in Birmingham. It was on CrystaLLM-Prop, where I fine-tuned the original CrystaLLM to predict a material’s band gap straight from its CIF, comparing next-token generation against a regression head on top of the model.

item.title: 1st place at the Energy Idea Challenge 2023
item.description: Prescelli Annan, Niklas Jutting, Tom Burns and I won first place at the Energy Idea Challenge 2023, sponsored by Octopus Energy, KPMG, Guidehouse and Imperial. Over a weekend, teams of students from Oxford, Cambridge, Imperial, UCL and other universities put together proposals to help the UK hit its net zero targets. Ours was a wastewater heat pump system, with machine learning for predictive maintenance.
